question.problem: Let $B={[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}$ and $C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ relative to the basis $C.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 4 & 8 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

On the right-hand side, we obtain the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
